study type: Case-control study with a validation cohort
outcome: Differentiation between necrotising enterocolitis (NEC) and highly suspected early onset food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (HSEO-FPIES)
cohort: Neonates diagnosed with necrotising enterocolitis (n=100), highly suspected early onset food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (n=71), and jaundice (control, n=62).
finding: Serum IL-27 levels were significantly higher in the NEC group than in the HSEO-FPIES group and demonstrated superior diagnostic efficiency (AUC=0.878) compared to other markers for differentiating NEC from HSEO-FPIES in neonates.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken at the time of diagnosis during the neonatal period.
